title: Model Zoo: find models and inspect their provenance
description: Open the nested model library, scan an existing local cache, and distinguish recorded training information from unknown provenance. Benchmarking is not demonstrated as successful while the current Cellpose argument incompatibility remains.
objectives: Find Model Zoo inside Make Masks and scan a local model directory.
Read source, kind, checksum and training-information fields without confusing unknown metadata with validation.
Distinguish model management from downloading, training and benchmarking.
prerequisite: spaCR 1.5.0.7 nightly. This real recording scans an existing Cellpose cache and selects the original cpsam checkpoint; it does not download, train or run inference. Use your own model directory rather than copying the presenter's home path. The selected checkpoint's metadata records no published checksum, training dataset or author; the tutorial does not infer those from its filename. A separate checksum establishes only that this local file stayed unchanged during recording, not that its origin is verified. Model Zoo's benchmark and Model Compare currently pass an unsupported invert keyword to Cellpose 4.2.1.1. That app-owned incompatibility is recorded separately and not repaired or bypassed here. See the Plaque tutorial for an actual model download and preview. No accuracy comparison or held-out validation is claimed.

scenes.narration: Model Zoo is the model library inside Make Masks. Open the host module, then use its Model Zoo control. This lesson demonstrates the real library and local model scan, not a new training run or an accuracy benchmark.

The table brings published entries and locally discovered files into one view. Read the model kind and source columns together. A model being listed does not mean it has been downloaded, tested on your images, or validated for your experiment.

Enter your existing model directory and press Scan, or choose a folder with the adjacent button. Here we scan the real Cellpose cache. Use your own path. Scanning discovers files and metadata; it does not train a model or run segmentation.

This scan displays eight entries. Some are published remote models and others are local checkpoints. The count describes this machine, not a required setup. Select the exact file you intend to use instead of assuming that similar model names identify the same weights.

The selected local checkpoint has no published checksum or recorded training provenance in this view. Unknown means unknown. Its name is not evidence of its training dataset. Our file checksum confirms that this recording left it unchanged; that does not establish who produced it or how well it performs.

The download area controls where an available remote model is saved. It also exposes a choice about models without published checksums; do not treat missing checksums as verified downloads. This local selection is not downloaded again. The Plaque lesson shows an actual model download and preview.

The lower area is for testing fields and comparing selected models. Those jobs are separate from scanning the library. The current Cellpose argument mismatch prevents us from claiming a successful benchmark here. No masks or test scores are fabricated. Keep representative validation images separate from training examples when evaluating a repaired workflow.
